title: "Gather" quote hoop in cross-stitch
subtitle: A single word in a block alphabet with a small floral flourish
excerpt: "Gather" is a 70-by-45 stitch word piece on 14-count Aida. The seven letters are stitched in a clean block alphabet in a warm terracotta, with a small sprig of wheat and berries worked below. Finished size is about 12.5 x 8 cm in a 15 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. Block alphabets for cross-stitch appear in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

content.text: . The seven letters are stitched in a 7-stitch-tall block alphabet in a single
colour (DMC 3830, terracotta). A small wheat-and-berry sprig sits below the word and introduces two more colours. Finished size is about 12.5 x 8 cm in a 15 cm hoop.

Text pieces require accurate letter spacing. Before stitching, count the total stitch width of all seven letters plus the four one-stitch gaps between them, then divide by two and mark the centre letter on the chart. Start from that centre letter rather than from the G on the left to ensure the word sits centred in the hoop.

items.name: 14-count Aida, cream or linen
items.substitutions: Natural linen Aida gives the terracotta palette a warm base

items.name: DMC floss
items.qty: 1 skein: 3830 (terracotta); 1 skein: 3012 (olive); 1 skein: 815 (dark red-brown for berries)

content.text: Count the full width of the word (letters plus gaps) and mark the centre stitch of the centre letter on both the chart and the fabric.
Stitch the letters from the centre outward, the middle of the T or H first, then the adjacent letters, then the G and R at the ends.
Work the wheat sprig and berry cluster below the word in the olive green (3012) and dark berry (815) once all letters are complete.
Wash gently and press face-down. Display in the hoop as finished art. The terracotta palette suits a warm-toned kitchen or hallway.

items.symptom: The lettering is misaligned: one word sits higher than the rest
items.cause: The word was started from a counted position relative to itself, not from the piece's centre mark.
items.fix: Mark the horizontal centre of the fabric and count outward from it for every word. Check that the baseline of each letter sits on the same counted row before stitching the first cross. Once the baselines are confirmed, alignment is guaranteed.

items.symptom: The decorative border does not close at the corners
items.cause: The border stitches were worked from one side rather than from opposite corners toward the middle.
items.fix: Start the border from each corner and work inward to the midpoints. Corners should be stitched first so the straight runs can be trimmed to fit. Once all four corners are in, the border joins should be invisible.

content.text: Once a single word feels easy, try the uppercase alphabet practice piece. It covers all 26 letters in one sampler and works as a reference for custom word pieces.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
